title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 12 board. The Eddies made it nine straight, 257.5–184 over the SPD's, and clinched a playoff spot at 9-2, Pocket dropped 298 for its fourth kitty and snapped a four-game skid, and Substation's Last Ride re-entry lasted one week after a 135.5 week floor, leaving four riders on the bus: the Eddies, Doubtpfizer, Hyper and Pocket. The Goats sit alone at 7-4 and five teams are stacked at 6-5. Tuesday's trades sent Rashee Rice from Doubtpfizer to Ultron for Omarion Hampton and Dallas Goedert from TTAB to the Eddies for Travis Etienne. Wednesday's waivers saw LAB spend $11 on Mike Green and Ja'Quan McMillian, Hyper add Xavier Watts and Konata Mumpfield, Doubtpfizer claim Antonio Johnson for $4, TTAB spend its last $3 on Zayne Anderson, Morningside claim Ted Hurst for $2, and Ultron add Jack Gibbens for $1. Nobody is on bye this week, Thanksgiving week kicks off Wednesday night with Green Bay at the Rams, and the Eddies host Pocket in a rider-against-rider showdown.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: nine straight after an 0-2 start, alone in first at 9-2, and a playoff spot clinched with three weeks to go. George Karlaftis' 37 led a 151 defense, best in the WU, with Jordyn Brooks and Frankie Luvu at 26 each, and Brock Purdy's 28 came in the 49ers' 35–10 win over Kirk Cousins' Vikings. The Eddies are still on the bus with $25 left. Junk: Michael Mayer scored 1.5 with Brock Bowers on IR, so Tuesday's trade sent Travis Etienne to TTAB for Dallas Goedert. Next is Pocket at home, the WU's points leader fresh off a 298 kitty, and it's rider against rider on the bus.

Juice: 298, the week's high, the fourth kitty of the season, and a 109.5-point win over the Goats that snapped a four-game skid. Jonah Coleman's 43 and CeeDee Lamb's 36 led a 176 offense, best in the WU, with Jared Goff at 30 and Will Anderson Jr. at 33 on the other side. Pocket leads the WU in points at 2974, 117.5 clear of Doubtpfizer, is still on the bus, and has $66, the fattest wallet. Junk: 2811 PA is the worst in the league, which is how the points leader is only 6-5. Next is a trip to the Eddies, nine straight and counting.

Juice: three straight. Dak Prescott's 49 was the top offensive score of the week, Nakobe Dean's 43 was second among IDPs, and Chuba Hubbard and Alex Singleton added 35 and 33 in a 268–206 win over LAB. Doubtpfizer is 6-5, second in PF at 2856.5, still on the bus, and has $64 after Wednesday's $4 claim on Antonio Johnson, second only to Pocket. Tuesday they sent Rashee Rice to Ultron for Omarion Hampton, so the backfield now runs six deep. Two titles in three years, and the stretch run looks familiar. Junk: Christian McCaffrey scored 14 a week after his 65, and 2797 PA is second-worst in the WU. The Dongers are next, fresh off 277, and Dak gets the Eagles on Thanksgiving.

Juice: still second at 7-4, a game clear of the five-team pile at 6-5. Patrick Mahomes scored 36, George Kittle 20.5 and Bucky Irving 20. Junk: Pocket beat them by 109.5, the biggest margin of the week, with DK Metcalf at 1, Amik Robertson at 0 and an 80-point defense. 2569 PF ranks ninth, and they're now two games back of first. The good news is the pattern: the Goats have alternated losses and wins for seven straight weeks, which makes Week 12 a win. Substation visits off the week floor, and Mahomes gets Buffalo on Thanksgiving night.

Juice: two straight and 6-5 after beating Hyper 238–193.5. Quinnen Williams' 44 was the top IDP score of the week, Dillon Thieneman added 26 and Caleb Downs 19 in a 148 defense, second only to the Eddies, and Javonte Williams and Jameson Williams scored 25 each. TTAB still has the stingiest PA in the WU at 2445, and Tuesday they turned Dallas Goedert into Travis Etienne, so Javonte finally has company at running back. Junk: Ryan Flournoy scored 2 and Mark Andrews 4, Wednesday they spent the last $3 on Zayne Anderson, so the wallet is empty, 2549 PF ranks 10th, and Bryce Young, the $7 bridge, got cut Saturday. Ultron visits on three straight.

Juice: three straight and 6-5 after a 223.5–201.5 win at Morningside. CJ Allen scored 35, Emmett Johnson 32 in his first week out of Hyper, and George Pickens 29. Tuesday's deal brought Rashee Rice from Doubtpfizer for Omarion Hampton, and with Kenneth Walker III out again, Emmett and Rice both go for the Chiefs in Buffalo on Thanksgiving night. Wednesday they claimed Jack Gibbens for $1, leaving $4. Junk: Kirk Cousins, the only quarterback on the roster, scored 3 in the Vikings' 35–10 loss to Brock Purdy's 49ers, while Antonio Williams' 27 and Mike Gesicki's 16.5 sat on the bench. 2502.5 PF ranks 11th. Next is a trip to TTAB and the stingiest PA in the league.

Juice: still 6-5, part of the five-team pile one game behind the Goats, and Tykee Smith's 24 led the defense. Junk: the Last Ride champion got back on the bus and lasted one week. Substation's 135.5 was the week floor, the offense managed 56.5 with Ja'Marr Chase at 8 and Jordyn Tyson at 1, Malcolm Rodriguez scored 20 on the bench, and Saltese, of all teams, sent them home 178–135.5. 2499 PF ranks 12th, and $4 is left. Next is a trip to the Goats, who haven't lost two in a row all season.

Juice: still on the bus, one of four riders left, and 2735.5 PF is fourth in the WU. Jacob Rodriguez scored 38 and A.J. Haulcy 26, and Bijan Robinson, who spent his first week in Hyper colors on Atlanta's bye, is back. Wednesday they claimed Xavier Watts for $1 and Konata Mumpfield for $3, leaving $2. Junk: two straight losses, the latest 238–193.5 to TTAB with Emeka Egbuka at 3 and an 80.5 offense, and at 5-6 Hyper is chasing from below .500. Kenneth Walker III is out again this week, and Lamar Jackson, stashed Sunday, is on IR with his thumb. Morningside visits on seven straight losses.

Juice: Jeffery Simmons scored 37, Cam Ward 30 and Jahmyr Gibbs 30, and 2701 PF is still fifth in the WU. Junk: 237 was the sixth-best score of the week and still lost to the Dongers by 40, a second straight loss that drops them to 5-6. Drake Maye's fractured ankle is why the quarterback room is Ward and Jacoby Brissett now, and Brissett scored 20 on the bench. The wallet is empty, so the wire has been a revolving door: Josh Cameron has been added three times and dropped twice since last Wednesday. The SPD's visit, and Gibbs gets the Bears on Thanksgiving.

Juice: 277, the second-best score of the week, and a 40-point win over the Slumlords. David Bailey scored 36, Joe Burrow 30, Chris Olave 27, Parker Washington 24 and D.J. Moore 23, and Burrow still leads the WU's offensive MVP race at 336, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba third at 318 and back from bye. That's four wins in five weeks after an 0-6 start, and 2661 PF ranks sixth. Junk: 4-7 with $1 left, and KaVontae Turpin's 23 and Ladd McConkey's 20 sat on the bench in a game they won anyway. Doubtpfizer visits on three straight.

Juice: Jeremiah Trotter scored 30 and Tyrel Dodson 28, Jordan Love is back from bye, and $40 is the third-fattest wallet. Junk: the Eddies beat them 257.5–184 to drop them to 5-6, with Bo Nix at 12, Jonathan Taylor at 7 and Andrew Van Ginkel at 4 while Danny Stutsman's 25, the $4 claim, sat on the bench. Nix got cut Tuesday with Love back, A.J. Brown and Davante Adams are both on IR, and Zaire Franklin is questionable for Green Bay's Wednesday night opener. Next is a trip to the Slumlords.

Juice: Ashton Jeanty scored 34 and Mike Evans 28, and $33 is left after Wednesday's $11 on Mike Green and Ja'Quan McMillian, the fourth-fattest wallet in the WU. Junk: five straight losses after a 5-1 start, the latest 268–206 at Doubtpfizer, with Jacob Parrish at 1 and Jaylen Warren, Caleb Douglas and Isaiah Likely at 5 each while Khalil Shakir's 21 and Jihaad Campbell's 19 sat on the bench. Saturday they cut Puka Nacua, who's on IR after MCL surgery and serving a three-game suspension. Next is a trip to Saltese, the other side of the Stroud and Jeanty trades.

Juice: they won, 178–135.5, and sent Substation's Last Ride re-entry right back off the bus. Jamien Sherwood scored 28, Jonas Sanker 24 and David Montgomery 23, and Saltese moves to 4-7. Junk: 178 was the second-lowest score of the week and still a win, M.J. Stewart scored 0 and Kyle Monangai 2, and Stewart and Ashton Dulin were both cut Tuesday. 2429.5 PF ranks 13th, and $2 is left. LAB visits on five straight losses, the team that sent over C.J. Stroud and took Ashton Jeanty.

Juice: Boye Mafe's 42 was the third-best IDP score of the week, Travis Kelce added 30.5, and the 22-point loss to Ultron was the closest game of the week. Wednesday they claimed Ted Hurst for $2 and added Deshaun Watson, leaving $3. Junk: seven straight losses, 3-8, and 2252 PF is last in the WU, 177.5 behind 13th. Terrel Bernard scored 3, and Xavier Worthy's 11 sat on the bench. They also dropped Aaron Rodgers a week after paying $1 to bring him back, so the quarterback room is Watson and Drew Lock now, which still matters with Seattle optimistic about Sam Darnold's return. Next is a trip to Hyper.
